The question of whether washing hair daily is harmful is genuinely contested, with experts and studies on both sides. A peer-reviewed study found that daily washing was superior to once-per-week cleansing with "no objective detrimental effects to hair" observed, and concluded that concerns about "overcleaning" were unfounded [d2]. A Unilever hair R&D expert similarly stated that "washing with a good shampoo and conditioner is not harmful to hair," leaving frequency up to the consumer [d13], and a licensed hairstylist and two medical experts (a trichologist and a dermatologist) echoed that daily shampooing is "not inherently bad" and can even be beneficial for scalp health [d1][d5].

On the other side, a dermatologist advises shampooing only 2–3 times per week, warning that "excessive shampooing deprives the scalp of its natural oils" [d8], and one source explicitly states that daily washing "is harmful to your hair and scalp," potentially causing dryness, split ends, breakage, dandruff, and thinning hair [d12]. Another source argues that "this very act of routine washing can actually harm hair in the long run" by stripping essential natural oils [d9], and a brief note from a barber-supply blog also warns that daily washing "may dry it out, resulting in dandruff and possible hair loss" [d10].

A middle-ground perspective suggests the answer depends on shampoo type and individual factors: daily washing "may not be harmful if you use the right shampoos," such as slightly acidic formulas, while high-pH shampoos should not be used daily [d4]. Overall, the evidence reflects genuinely conflicting expert opinions and research outcomes, with no single universal answer applicable to all hair types and products [d2][d12].
